what: GSK is a British pharmaceutical company. It develops medicines for HIV, respiratory disease and cancer, and is one of the world's largest vaccine makers, with shingles, meningitis and respiratory vaccines.
customers: Health systems, insurers, pharmacies and governments worldwide.
money: HIV treatments, respiratory biologics and oncology
shingles, meningitis, RSV and flu vaccines
moat: Patent-protected medicines and a vaccine manufacturing base that takes a decade and billions to replicate.
risks: Shingrix vaccine sales have been weaker than expected
Patents on its HIV medicines expire later this decade
US litigation over the heartburn medicine Zantac has been a long overhang
Debt of about $31 billion against modest cash
opportunities: Revenue grew about 12% last year with a 72% gross margin
Return on invested capital near 20% is strong for a large pharmaceutical company
A pipeline weighted toward respiratory and oncology medicines in late-stage trials
watch: Vaccine sales and late-stage trial readouts in oncology and respiratory.
